metadata.note: The Milwaukee Road's North Montana Line, built Harlowton-Lewistown-Great Falls in 1913-14 and the second railroad to reach Great Falls with passenger trains. Its Great Falls depot of 1915 still stands. Passenger service lasted just over forty years: the depot stopped handling passengers on Dec 1 1954 and the trains were gone by August 1955, a decade before the Great Northern gave up its own Great Falls services. Most of the line is abandoned; the Moccasin-Geraldine section survives as Central Montana Rail.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_station (the Milwaukee Road built the North Montana Line from Harlowton to Great Falls in 1913-14; Geraldine depot 1914; daily freight and passenger trains; passenger service ended 1955; the line went to Burlington Northern in 1980, closed by a landslide in 1982, and was bought by Central Montana Rail in 1985).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Falls_station (the Milwaukee's 1915 Great Falls depot served passengers until Dec 1 1954, when ticketing moved to the Great Northern station; passenger service to Great Falls ceased by August 1955; the station infobox places Great Falls on the "Northern Montana Division" between Falls Yard, toward Harlowton, and Manchester, toward Agawam).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_Railroad (the Montana Railroad, "the Jawbone", was built Lombard-Lewistown 1895-1903, reached Harlowton in 1900 and Lewistown in 1903, and was bought by the Milwaukee Road in 1908; the Harlowton-Lewistown route became a Milwaukee secondary main line, later extended to Great Falls).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Montana_Rail,_Inc. (Central Montana Rail runs 84.2 miles Moccasin-Geraldine, most of it originally the Milwaukee Road's "Northern Montana" line to Great Falls; the southern 19.6 miles Moccasin-Kingston Junction were built by the Great Northern as part of its Lewistown branch).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways and speed are estimates; no Milwaukee Road timetable was consulted, and no train name or numbers were found for this service. The 1930 segment boundary is editorial. SOURCE CONFLICT: the Great Falls station article's infobox gives the station as "Opened 1908", which cannot be squared with the same article's (and the Geraldine article's) 1913-14 construction of the line -- 1908 is the year the Milwaukee's Pacific Extension crossed Montana and the year it bought the Montana Railroad. This layer draws 1914, the year the track reached Great Falls. NOT DRAWN: the Milwaukee's extension beyond Great Falls northwest to Agawam, opened about 1916, over which the same passenger trains ran (the Great Falls station infobox names Manchester as the next stop toward Agawam). OpenStreetMap's trackage between Great Falls and Choteau is a mixture of ex-Great Northern and ex-Milwaukee alignments and could not be told apart with confidence, and a trace that ran up the Great Northern's Sun River branch instead would be exactly the era-mismatch error CLAUDE.md Rule 2 warns about. Also not drawn: Harlowton-Lewistown before 1914, when it was the Montana Railroad and then a Milwaukee branch but not yet part of a Great Falls route.

Overpass API (maps.mail.ru mirror), bbox dump of every railway way between Great Falls, Lewistown and Harlowton, pulled 2026-08-26. Endpoints are the OSM place nodes for Harlowton, Lewistown and Great Falls.

segments.note: The Milwaukee Road built its North Montana Line from Harlowton to Great Falls in 1913-14, striking northwest from its own Pacific Extension main line to reach the largest city in the state that it did not already serve. The Harlowton-Lewistown half was older -- the Montana Railroad, the "Jawbone", had reached Lewistown in 1903 and was bought by the Milwaukee in 1908 -- and the 137 miles from Lewistown northwest to Great Falls were laid in 1914. Daily freight and passenger trains served the new homestead towns along it. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_station ("In 1913-14, The Milwaukee Road built the North Montana Line from Harlowton, Montana to Great Falls, Montana"; the Geraldine depot was built 1914 and "daily freight and passenger trains stopped there"); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_Railroad (the Montana Railroad reached Lewistown in 1903 and was purchased by the Milwaukee Road in 1908; the Harlowton-Lewistown route became a Milwaukee secondary main line, later extended to Great Falls). Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Traffic fell away after the Second World War. The Milwaukee's own Great Falls depot -- a 1915 building with a 135-foot tower, hailed as the finest between Spokane and Chicago -- stopped handling passengers on Dec 1 1954, when the railroad moved its ticketing and boarding to the Great Northern station; by August 1955 the Milwaukee had given up passenger service to Great Falls entirely. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Falls_station (the Milwaukee depot "continued to serve passengers until December 1, 1954, when the Milwaukee Road began ticketing and boarding at the nearby Great Northern station" and "By August 1955 the Milwaukee Road had ceased passenger service to Great Falls", citing the Great Falls Tribune of Nov 17 1954 and Aug 9 1955); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_station ("passenger serv[ice] ended in 1955"). The 1930 start of this segment is editorial, and the headway is an estimate.
